chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from Ja'far b. Salama al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad. He said: al-Qinad narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Hashim b. al-Burayd narrated to us from his father. He said:

Zayd b. Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about the saying of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family): "Whoever takes me as a master, then Ali is his master." He said: He set him up as a sign so that the Party of Allah may be known through him at the time of the split.

key_terms.الفرقة: The split, division — the factional divisions that arose in the Muslim community after the Prophet's death
key_terms.حزب الله: The Party of Allah — the community of true believers aligned with divine guidance (cf. Quran 58:22)
key_terms.علم: Sign, standard, banner — a distinguishing mark by which something is known
key_terms.مولى: Master, guardian, patron — the central term of the Ghadir hadith, denoting authority and leadership

ai.seo_question: What did Zayd b. Ali say about the meaning of the Ghadir hadith 'man kuntu mawlahu fa Ali mawlahu'?
ai.summary: Zayd b. Ali, the grandson of Imam al-Husayn, was asked about the meaning of the Prophet's famous Ghadir declaration "Whoever takes me as a master, then Ali is his master." He explained that the Prophet appointed Ali as a distinguishing standard (alam) by which the true Party of Allah could be identified when the Muslim community would fracture after the Prophet's passing. This interpretation frames the Ghadir declaration not merely as a personal commendation of Ali but as a divinely ordained mechanism for preserving the identity of the righteous community.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
so that it may be known

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from Ja`far b. Salama al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad. He said: Al-Qinad narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Hashim b. Burayd narrated to us from his father. He said:

Zayd b. `Ali (as) was asked about the saying of the Messenger of Allah (s): “Whoever takes me as a Master, then `Ali is his Master.” He said: He set him up as a sign so that it may be known through him who the Party of Allah were during the split.
